To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the chemokine system is a complex signaling network involving multiple receptors that are capable of interacting with each other and with other receptors.
Chemokine receptors form homo- and hetero-oligomers that are functionally important.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of signal transduction by G-protein coupled receptors.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the control of immune cell trafficking.
the mechanisms by which chemokine receptors are modulated by dimerization and/or crosstalk.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chemokine receptor signaling is a complex and dynamic process, and it is the interplay of these various signaling pathways that is responsible for the diversity in cellular responses.
chemokines and chemokine receptors are not isolated players but are part of complex signaling networks.
there is a lot more to learn about the regulation of chemokine receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chemokine receptors are not only the target of the chemokines but also the target of the other receptors, such as the G protein-coupl...

the integration of signals downstream from chemokine receptors, including crosstalk with receptors and other signaling systems, is key to understanding the fine tuning of cellular responses, and that these processes are important in the context of drug development.
chemokine receptor dimerization can be a mechanism for modulating receptor activity and that this activity can also be regulated by other signaling pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is a complex network of interactions between chemokine receptors that are critical for their function and that these interactions can have significant effects on the function of chemokine receptors.
the activity of chemokine receptors is modulated by their interactions with other receptors and signaling pathways.

chemokine receptors can be modulated by dimerization and by crosstalk with signaling pathways, and that the consequences of these interactions can be both beneficial and detrimental to health and disease.
